_meta.purpose: Converged-panel/persistent-floor misroute: the panel converged to 0 blocking by round 2, yet the loop kept re-entering code-grade and the counting guard halted at re-entry 3 with max 2. Under the whole-lap rule the converged laps waive and the run continues. Carries lap 1 code-confirm row (the post-confirm fold reads it — round 1 run extends through the confirm verdict) and the snapshot-less pre-P2e topology (no code-snapshot rows exist in this run; code-fix rows close the rounds).
_meta.excerpt_rule: Trail lines 64-95 in verbatim order: every code-cite-check row, every code-grade unit row, lap 1 code-confirm row, the three code-fix rows (round delimiters), all routing rows, and the halt row. No code-demote or code-snapshot rows exist in this range.
_meta.channel_rule: Each stage row bakes its outcome channel in `channel` (derived from the workflow's outcome map so the replay needs no workflow introspection): code-cite-check->code-cite-check; code-grade/code-confirm->code-verdicts; code-snapshot->code-snapshot; code-fix->plans. code-demote publishes no channel and its rows are dropped.
_meta.trim_rule: Stage rows keep stageNumber/stage/channel plus the fold-read fields only: verdict rows (code-grade units + code-confirm) keep dimension/pass/severity/artifact and findings trimmed to the first finding {detail} (the anchor-nit clamp inside the blocking predicate reads findings; on this trail the clamp never decides a recorded count — every blocking verdict is pass:false severity medium, every waived one passes or sits at low/none); cite-check rows keep dimension/pass/severity; snapshot rows keep their prior fs handle; code-fix rows keep the plans fs handle + phase_count. Dropped: score/graded_at/feedback/kind/meta/ts, risk_rulings (the blocking predicate is risk-blind), verdict rows own artifacts array. Routing rows keep type/fromStage/decision verbatim. The halt row is normalized to the new kind {type:halt,stage,errMsg} with errMsg verbatim.
_meta.row_format: compact one-row-per-line JSON (each rows[] element on a single line)

findings.detail: Goal R6.3 requires the 16-char Header cap note be stated 'wherever skills instruct checkpoint questions (research, design-slice, implement advisor/checkpoint sections, or the shared _shared prompt fragment if one exists)'. design-slice is EXPLICITLY NAMED in that scope, and packages/rpiv-pi/skills/design-slice/SKILL.md:63 instructs ask_user_question ('Use ask_user_question (2-4 concrete options, one at a time) ONLY when you cant settle it from those inputs') — so it constructs a Header at runtime and is in scope. But Phase 8 scoped itself to 'each of the 13 Header-emitting skill files' (files showing an explicit Header:/Header example value), a narrower proxy that silently excludes design-slice (which shows no Header example yet still issues one). design-slice appears NOWHERE in the plan (verified by grep) and Phase 8's Notes/Deferred never documents the exclusion. This silently drops an explicitly-named goal ask: a model following design-slice can construct a >16-char Header and hit the exact schema-validation failure (~40s retry, the motivating incident) that R6.3 exists to prevent. Fix: add design-slice/SKILL.md as a 14th file to Phase 8's files set, inserting the canonical cap line adjacent to the design-slice:63 ask_user_question instruction; alternatively document an explicit deferral with a reason (none exists today).

Phase 3 intro cites planGatePasses/codeGatePasses at :2382/:2389 (its own 'corrected' text), but they actually sit at :2386/:2393 in built-in-workflows.ts. Informational only: the plan states these are NOT modified here (they call allRiskFlagsPass transitively), so no edit anchor depends on the line numbers, and the fold rewires that ARE load-bearing (RiskRuling :2321, verdictRiskRulings :2327, allRiskFlagsPass :2345, dimensionsToRegrade clause 3 :2189-2190, confirmDue riskFail :2426) all resolve exactly as cited.

Goal R6.3 explicitly names design-slice as a checkpoint-question skill ('State the limit wherever skills instruct checkpoint questions (research, design-slice, implement advisor/checkpoint sections, or the shared _shared prompt fragment if one exists)'). design-slice/SKILL.md:63 instructs ask_user_question ('Use ask_user_question (2-4 concrete options, one at a time) ONLY when you can't settle it from those inputs'), and ask_user_question requires a header field capped at 16 chars, so design-slice constructs a Header at runtime and is in scope. But Phase 8 scoped itself to 'the 13 Header-emitting skill files' (files showing an explicit Header: example value), a narrower proxy that silently excludes design-slice (which shows no Header example yet still issues one). Verified: grep for 'design-slice' across the entire plan returns ZERO matches; Phase 8's frontmatter files set lists 13 files including design/SKILL.md (a DIFFERENT skill, confirmed by their distinct SKILL.md descriptions) but NOT design-slice/SKILL.md; Phase 8's Notes/Deferred covers placement convention, grammar variants, and per-template guarding (risk c8r1) but never mentions design-slice or documents the exclusion. This silently drops an explicitly-named goal ask: a model following design-slice can construct a >16-char Header and hit the exact schema-validation failure (~40s retry) that R6.3 exists to prevent. The goal's other R6.3-named scopes are covered (research at :172, implement at :71) and the _shared clause does not apply (packages/rpiv-pi/skills/_shared holds only .mjs helpers + .test.ts, no checkpoint/ask_user_question/Header references).

The Phase 5 snapshot-stage publish-contract test block is emitted with a mis-indented closing: the expect(...) wrapping call's closing paren and the .toThrow(...) chain land flush-left at column 0 rather than aligning under the expect. Biome --write (run by this phase's own scoped #### Automated Verification:) rewrites it before commit, so execution is not impeded, but the code block as written in the plan is not byte-identical to what the file will contain post-format.

The new body-scanning helpers (Phase 1 reconciliationRecords/planVerificationCommands and Phase 5 sectionIndexOf) use inline regex literals for the generic heading-open/close markers (/^#{1,4}\s/, /^##\s/, /^####\s+Reconciliation\b/) where the module also has a precedent for named module-level heading RegExp constants (PLAN_PHASE_RE :73, REVIEW_PHASE_RE :400, SLICE_HEADING_RE :817). This is cosmetic, not behavioral: the module already uses inline regexes liberally (the fence regex /^\s*(`{3,}|~{3,})/ is inline in all three existing copies), and the plan DOES declare named constants for its directive grammars (RECONCILE_DIRECTIVE_RE, AV_COMMAND_LINE_RE, TEST_PATH_RE), so it follows the stronger precedent where a matcher is reused and inlines the one-shot generic markers. Flagged only as a consistency nudge, not a divergence that blocks.

A few test-file navigation line-numbers drift by 1-7 lines from the live tree while the surrounding anchor TEXT is exact, so the edits remain executable. Examples: the adaptive gate scaling block is cited at built-in-workflows.ts:3414 but the describe actually opens at :3407; the gradePanelFanout JSDoc opening is cited at :2194 and dimensionsToRegrade's closing }; at :2193, whereas the }; sits at :2192 and the /** at :2194; the implement/SKILL.md Reconciliation region is summarized as :33 but the 'Do not read, edit, or check off other phases' bullet it anchors on is at :36. Every one of these gives the exact anchor text (test/describe names or code lines) which I verified matches the tree, so the navigation drift is cosmetic only.

Phase 2's validate-workflow-invariant.mjs (under skills/elaborate/_helpers/) imports extension internals (built-in-workflows.ts, skill-contracts-source.ts, outcome-derivation.ts, paths.ts) via jiti -- verified it is the FIRST skills-layer file to depend on extensions/rpiv-core (grep across packages/rpiv-pi/skills/ found zero existing imports of extensions/rpiv-core today). This completes a bidirectional intra-package coupling, since the reverse direction already exists (extensions/rpiv-core/paths.ts exports BUNDLED_SKILLS_DIR pointing at skills/, and buildSkillContractsFromFrontmatter reads skill frontmatter). The choice is defensible -- a read-only probe mirroring built-in-workflows.test.ts, within the same npm package (no package boundary crossed, and the documented zero-cross-imports rule is about sibling extension packages, not within-package layering) -- but it is a new dependency direction the plan records only as a jiti-resolution risk (c2r3), not as an explicit layering decision. Worth a one-line acknowledgement that skills->extensions is a new intra-package edge.

Phase 2's validate-workflow-invariant.mjs introduces a novel layering coupling: it jiti-loads four rpiv-core INTERNAL (non-exported) modules (built-in-workflows.ts, skill-contracts-source.ts, outcome-derivation.ts, paths.ts) via relative-path resolution from a skill helper. No existing skills/_shared/*.mjs loads extension internals — they import only node: builtins (stitch-elaborations.mjs:29-31). The plan reaches non-exported extension internals through relative paths rather than a declared export surface (it even notes exporting the helpers would be an un-enumerated API change, yet achieves the same coupling via path resolution). It does NOT cross a forbidden boundary (rpiv-pi skills -> rpiv-pi extensions is intra-package; rpiv-pi -> rpiv-workflow is already an established PRODUCTION direction -- built-in-workflows.ts:45-46 imports @juicesharp/rpiv-workflow/registration + /runner; jiti is a declared dep of rpiv-pi at package.json:67), so it is not a blocking conflict -- but it diverges from the established skill-helper pattern (pure node: imports) and is fragile to rpiv-core path-layout changes. Explicitly flagged as risk c2r3; minimal mechanism for the route-reads-unvalidated-data defect class. Architecturally sound direction + boundary; novel coupling, low impact.

Goal R1.1 explicitly requires reconcile to 'run the plan's final whole-plan Automated Verification block (reconcile becomes its first reader; validate re-runs it as the independent check)'. The plan's reconcile instead re-runs every PER-PHASE #### Automated Verification: command (planVerificationCommands, H4-scoped) and never the whole-plan npm test / npm run check block. Substantive whole-plan coverage is preserved (validate still runs it, and per-phase tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.base.json IS a whole-program check), and the R1 acceptance-criterion outcome ('whole-plan block goes green, validate passes') still holds, so this is a mechanism divergence rather than a contradiction; recorded because the named reconcile responsibility is unmet as literally specified.
